english.title: Liquidator fail to produce and send progress report
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a liquidator, failed, in respect of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..),

(A)_[for a prescribed period, namely **(..SPECIFY PERIOD..), to produce a progress report relating to the prescribed matters]_
(B)_[within the period of **(..SPECIFY PERIOD..) commencing with the end of the prescribed period, to produce a progress report, to send that progress report to the members of the company and such other persons as were prescribed]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 92A of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
liquidator fail to produce progress report relating to prescribed matters
or send a copy of it to members of the company or prescribed persons
within such period commencing with the end of the prescribed period

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.
